options.description: Draw with ASCII only. Defaults to what `unicodeSupported()` says of `env` and `platform`, since block elements and braille are not safe where box drawing is not.
options.name: ascii

options.description: The width of a vertical bar, and so of its column. Defaults to the widest label or value, so that neither is cut -- unless the bars would then be wider than `width`, when it is narrowed until they are not.
options.name: barWidth

options.description: `horizontal` bars grow rightwards, `vertical` upwards. Defaults to `horizontal`.
options.name: direction

options.description: The environment to read the terminal from. Defaults to `process.env`.
options.name: env

options.description: How a number is written. Defaults to at most two decimals. A style in what it returns is dropped, and the value is drawn as plain text: a chart is coloured by its role, not by a string.
options.name: format

options.description: The columns between one vertical bar and the next. Defaults to 1.
options.name: gap

options.description: How tall a vertical chart is, in rows, which defaults to 8; and the most rows a horizontal chart is drawn in, which defaults to 1,000. A horizontal chart that has more bars than this shows some of them, as a vertical one does when it has more bars than columns -- the latest, unless `keep` says the first -- and the scale is over the bars shown.
options.name: height

options.description: Which end of the list is shown when the chart has more bars than it has room for: `last` keeps the latest bars and drops the first, as a sparkline keeps its latest samples; `first` keeps the first bars and drops the rest, which is what a list sorted largest first wants. The scale is over the bars shown either way. Defaults to `last`. The first of an object is the first of its keys, which JavaScript lists integer-like keys ascending before any others: a ranked list is an array of `{ label, value }` or a `Map`, which keep the order they were written in.
options.name: keep

options.description: The widest a label may be before it is cut. Defaults to its own width.
options.name: labelWidth

options.description: The value drawn as the top. Defaults to the largest value.
options.name: max

options.description: The value drawn as the bottom. Defaults to the smallest value.
options.name: min

options.description: The platform to detect for. Defaults to `process.platform`.
options.name: platform

options.description: Which role colours the data. Defaults to `accent`.
options.name: role

options.description: Whether to write each value. Defaults to true.
options.name: showValues

options.description: The widest the chart may be. Defaults to `terminalWidth()` for a horizontal chart, and to the terminal's own width for a vertical one. A vertical chart that has more bars than this has columns for shows the latest of them, as a sparkline shows its latest samples -- or the first, with `keep: 'first'`: bars are narrowed to fit first, down to a column each, and only then dropped from the left, or from the right.
options.name: width
